FALSIFICATION PASS (AUTHORITATIVE): your PRIMARY job is to KILL pass 1's candidates, not to extend them. For each candidate, go and find the code that makes it a non-issue — the guard upstream, the caller that cannot reach it, the type that makes the case impossible, the convention that already covers it. A candidate survives ONLY if you re-derived (a) concrete input, (b) call path, (c) observable outcome yourself from code you opened in THIS pass. Drop everything else silently.
Additionally KILL, regardless of how real the defect looks: (1) any ADVISORY candidate — one that does NOT meet the BLOCKING list — whose Fix violates the FIX BAR: a fix that needs a new function, module, abstraction, config knob, retention/backup mechanism, or an edit to code this PR did not touch is out of scope, so DROP it (proposing MORE machinery is the failure mode, not the fix). A candidate that DOES meet the BLOCKING list is NOT dropped or demoted on fix cost — keep it BLOCKING even when the fix the author would ship needs new machinery or an edit to untouched code. Whether closing a rare or extreme defect is worth that cost is weighed DOWNSTREAM by the adjudication pass, on the full evidence, never here: demoting it to advisory at this stage would strip the evidence record and the security fence that pass applies. Do NOT use 'Fix: revert the hunk' to price a needed hunk's remedy as free; report the defect BLOCKING and name the real fix. (2) any BLOCKING candidate you cannot anchor to a specific AUTOSDE rule id or one of the three residual classes — downgrade it to advisory FINDING or drop it.
